method.question: Are relatively large primary-dealer awards at regular nominal ten-year Treasury auctions followed by a larger or more persistent change in aggregate coupon inventories?
method.award: Primary dealers’ competitive par award divided by the competitive par awarded inside the offering. Official competitive bidder classes reconcile to this denominator. All regular new issues and reopenings are retained; the June 2019 contingency test is excluded.
method.groups: Rank all awards in each reporting period and issue type. The bottom and top thirds use inclusive linearly interpolated 1/3 and 2/3 cut-offs. The cut-offs use each full sample period and are retrospective.
method.timing: Baseline is the last Wednesday strictly before auction. Settlement is the first Wednesday on or after issue. Later observations use exact weekly offsets and are omitted at a reporting break or from the next regular ten-year auction onward. Pre-trend is the prior Wednesday. Pre-settlement is the last Wednesday strictly before issue and can include the auction.
method.units: Awards are at par. Weekly positions use market value, in USD billions, for nominal Treasury coupons with more than seven and no more than eleven years remaining. Net equals outright long less short. The Fed’s trade-date series includes when-issued trading and auction allotments on the award date.
method.interpretation: The weekly maturity bucket contains other securities, valuation changes and secondary trades. Its change can reflect a short being covered. Trade timing, unrelated flows and shared market conditions leave the holding period of a particular security unidentified.
method.release: FR 2004A Wednesday observations are normally released the following Thursday, at least eight days later, and may be revised.

sameSecurity.method: At a regular reopening the same nominal ten-year note is already trading. Match its CUSIP using the Treasury schedule of original ten-year issues on each observation date. For the first Wednesday on or after issue and subsequent Wednesdays, subtract the last Wednesday strictly before issue. Keep observations in the same reporting period before the next regular ten-year auction. Source data aggregate all dealers’ net settled positions in the current issue at par, in millions of US dollars. Changes can reflect short covering or secondary-market trading. The public series does not tag individual dealers or lots.
